talking_points.headline: HSBC’s deposit mix figures add context to wealth and funding choices
talking_points.context_html: Elhedery said Hong Kong term deposits rose to 38% of the deposit mix from 36%, largely on new deposits, while he also described Asian wealth as an investment priority. A useful change-execution question is how client journeys and service capacity would accommodate customers moving between deposit and wealth needs. The article does not specify the period for the deposit figures or detail any resulting internal work.

talking_points.headline: Ebury’s proposed Singapore expansion depends on licensing and operating readiness
talking_points.context_html: Ebury has in-principle approvals for expanded payment services and corporate FX hedging, subject to MAS conditions and final approval expected in the first half of 2027. If those services proceed, local compliance and operations staffing will be dependencies alongside product build and client onboarding. The report describes planned capabilities, not a currently available service.

HSBC News.title: HSBC CEO Sees Deposit Growth and Asian Wealth as Bank Bets on AI
HSBC News.summary: HSBC CEO Georges Elhedery discussed deposit competition, Asian wealth investment, AI and organizational simplification at a JPMorgan conference. The report adds figures including Hong Kong deposits growing about 10% ($68 billion) and term deposits rising to 38% of the deposit mix from 36%; these details sharpen the competitive and delivery context, but the article does not specify the period for several deposit and lending figures or describe implementation plans.

Private Banking & Wealth.title: Singapore Assets Under Management Reach SGD7 Trillion, Minister of State Alvin Tan Tells HSBC Wealth Summit
Private Banking & Wealth.summary: At the inaugural HSBC Singapore Wealth Investment Summit, Minister of State Alvin Tan said Singapore assets under management had reached SGD7 trillion and private-banking client assets had grown about 50% over five years. He also highlighted trust, innovation and philanthropy as priorities for the wealth centre and said AI could reduce time spent gathering information and preparing investment recommendations; this signals a public policy and market context for wealth delivery, not a specific HSBC commitment or implementation plan.

Regulatory & Markets.title: Why Did an HSBC Whistleblower Urge a Probe of Correspondent Banking After the Deutsche Bank Leak?
Regulatory & Markets.summary: A former HSBC compliance officer, Everett Stern, urged US officials to investigate correspondent-banking flows after the publication of Deutsche Bank documents, alleging that HSBC may have carried some related funds through its correspondent division in 2010. The report describes allegations and historical material, not a finding against HSBC; the practical control question is how institutions maintain visibility across multi-bank payment chains, while the article does not establish HSBC’s involvement in the activity described.

Competitor Intelligence.title: Ebury Secures Two In-Principle Approvals from MAS for Singapore Expansion
Competitor Intelligence.summary: Ebury received two in-principle MAS approvals for an expanded Singapore payment scope and a Capital Markets Services licence, subject to final approval expected in the first half of 2027. The proposed permissions would support corporate FX hedging, multi-currency e-wallets and virtual collection accounts; any launch would depend on satisfying MAS conditions and building local compliance and operations capacity.

AI & Technology.title: MAS and SFA Name 11 Winners of 2026 FinTech Awards at Singapore FinTech Festival
AI & Technology.summary: MAS and the Singapore FinTech Association announced 11 winners across the 2026 Global FinTech Hackcelerator and SFF FinTech Excellence Awards. This report adds that the Hackcelerator drew 195 applications from 52 jurisdictions; the awards offer examples for technology and compliance delivery, but recognition and possible pilot opportunities do not establish broad deployment or proven outcomes.
